en: The Hymn of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Glorious Āñjaneya, from the *Kālikā-rahasya*.
The great hero Āñjaneya Hanumān, son of the Wind-god, is the bestower of the knowledge of reality and the giver of the mudrā of the goddess Sītā. || 1 ||
The destroyer of the Aśoka grove, the dispeller of all illusions, the liberator from all bonds, and the one who brings about the destruction of the Rākṣasas. || 2 ||
It is the warder-off of hostile sciences, the destroyer of the prowess of others, the repeller of enemy mantras, and the breaker of the mechanisms of adversaries. || 3 ||
He is the destroyer of all seizing spirits, the one who acts as an ally to Bhīmasena;
he removes all suffering, wanders through all worlds, and is swift as thought.
Seated at the foot of the Pārijāta tree, he possesses the nature of all mantras,
embodies the nature of all tantras, and likewise consists of the essence of all yantras.
The Lord of Monkeys, of massive body, is the Master who removes all diseases;
he bestows the perfection of strength and grants the wealth of all vidyās. || 6 ||
And he shall be the leader of the monkey army, possessing four faces like Brahmā,
a celibate youth, and radiant with jeweled earrings.
Resplendent with twelve flickering, bound,
and hanging crests, he was a knower of the reality of the Gandharva-vidyās, possessing great strength and prowess.
He is the liberator from prison and the releaser from the bonds of chains;
he is the wise one who enables crossing the ocean, the messenger of Rāma, and the majestic one.
The monkey, son of Kesari, who dispels the grief of Sita;
born from the womb of Anjana, his face resembles the rising sun. || 10 ||
He who acts for the pleasure of Vibhīṣaṇa, the destroyer of the lineage of the Ten-necked one, the giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa, possessing a body of diamond and great splendor. || 11 ||
Long-lived, a devotee of Rāma, an obstructor of the Daityas' works, a slayer of Akṣa, golden-hued, five-faced, and a great ascetic. || 12 ||
The glorious destroyer of Laṅkinī, the slayer of Siṃhikā’s life-breath,
who dwells on Mount Gandhamādana and set the city of Laṅkā ablaze.
The wise minister of Sugrīva, a hero who is the destroyer of the Daitya race, honored by the gods, possessed of great splendor, and the bestower of the crest-jewel upon Rāma. (14)
Capable of assuming any form at will, with tawny eyes, he was honored by Maināka as he crossed the ocean; having conquered his senses, he had swallowed the orb of the sun.
The unifier of Rāma and Sugrīva, the crusher of the great Rāvaṇa, radiant as crystal, the lord of speech, and a scholar of the nine grammatical systems. || 16 ||
The four-armed one, the kinsman of the distressed, the Great Soul, compassionate toward his devotees;
the remover of the Sañjīvana tree, pure, eloquent, and firm in his vows. || 17 ||
The destroyer of Kālanemi; the monkey-like Hari who is himself a monkey; the self-controlled, the tranquil, the one whose soul is serene; the remover of the pride of Śatakaṇṭha. 18.
A yogi eager for the story of Rāma, skilled in the search for Sītā, with adamantine tusks and adamantine claws, born from the prowess of Rudra. || 19 ||
He is the repeller of the unerring Brahmāstra weapon discharged by Indrajit;
he dwells upon the tip of Arjuna’s banner and is the piercer of the cage of arrows.
Ten-armed, worshiped by the world, increasing the joy of Jāmbavat, he is the bearer of the burden of worship for Śrī Rāmabhadra who is united with Sītā. || 21 ||
Thus ends the one hundred and eight names of the illustrious Hanumān.
Whoever should read or listen to this constantly shall obtain all desires.
Thus ends the hymn of one hundred and eight names of the illustrious Āñjaneya.
